judgment_calls_flagged_for_reviewer: expr.ex line ~221 (Rules 2/3 rewrite comment inside a `cond do` branch, citing transition.zig:1177/:1183) sits inside a bare Elixir `#` comment block, not a @moduledoc heredoc or .md file. Following REQ-243's established precedent exactly, the marker there is prefixed '# ' to keep the file syntactically valid, while remaining substring-greppable by the design's own regex.

expr.ex's 'Sentinel result...' @typedoc (originally 1 paragraph read as unit) actually contains two blank-line-separated sub-paragraphs, the second (REVIEWER GATE / OQ-1 RESOLVED text) also citing evaluator.zig. Initially only the first sub-paragraph got a marker; a residual-scan pass (mirroring REQ-243's own awk verification method) caught this and a second marker was added to the second sub-paragraph. Flagging because it's a reminder that a @typedoc/@moduledoc heredoc can contain multiple citation units separated by internal blank lines, same as ordinary prose -- the design doc's paragraph-unit rule applies per-blank-line-bounded-paragraph even inside one heredoc, not once per heredoc.

pin_resolver.ex: two paragraphs sit between marked citation units and do NOT themselves carry a .zig substring even though they discuss the same OQ-1/override topic and are physically adjacent to marked paragraphs (the OQ-1 second sub-paragraph, lines 131-151 in the final file, which is where the pin_resolver.ex:141->145 divergence line 'unlike R-Co's structural inability...' lives, and the override_entry @typedoc's own body after its first line). These were deliberately left unmarked since they cite only .md paths (ISS-0079/0078 design docs), not .zig -- confirmed by direct grep, not by inference from proximity.

pin_resolver.ex and expr.ex both needed a second/third marker beyond what an initial single read-through of the file located, purely because a moduledoc/typedoc heredoc's internal blank-line-separated sub-paragraphs are easy to under-count on a first pass. Recommend REVIEWER (or a doc-completeness follow-up to req237's own design doc, same idea as REQ-243's reviewer noted for the bare-#-comment case) call out explicitly that a heredoc is not one citation unit merely because it's one string -- each of its blank-line-bounded paragraphs is its own unit, same as plain Markdown.
